Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Acme renewal — Dedicated GPU right-sizing & proposed add-on plan

Hi Lisa,

Following up on our renewal conversation: attached is a short utilization extract (acme_utilization_q1-2026.csv) and a one-page proposal for how we can right-size your Dedicated pool while keeping headroom for peak inference. Key takeaways from the data:

- Average GPU utilization over the last 90 days: ~58%
- Peak daily tail utilizes ~92% of current committed vGPUs during business hours (PST)
- Dynamic burst events (nightly batch scoring) cause short-duration spikes that drive queuing

Proposal summary:
1) Reduce base committed GPUs from 64 -> 56 (expected to save ~12% on monthly reserved cost)
2) Add a 12-GPU burst pool attached to the same tenant to handle peak and nightly batches
3) Keep current autoscale ceiling at 80 GPUs for short-term mitigation while we observe behavior for one renewal cycle

Ask: can we set up a 30-minute call next week to walk through the numbers and draft the renewal amendment? I included Dev and Marissa for sizing and pricing details.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
--
Attachment: acme_utilization_q1-2026.csv (CSV, 78KB)

Monica — thanks for the quick analysis, this looks helpful. A few clarifying questions before scheduling:

1) How did you calculate the "peak daily tail" figure? Is that based on a single busiest hour or aggregated bursts?
2) What latency/SLAs do we expect to maintain if base committed GPUs go down to 56? We need to avoid user-facing latency regressions for the recommender service.
3) Can the burst pool be pre-warmed so we avoid cold-start latency for the nightly scoring jobs?

I can take a 30-minute slot on Wednesday afternoon PST. Adding Procurement to the loop to surface any PO lead time constraints.

Best,
Lisa
Sr. ML Infra Manager, Acme Corporation

Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 08:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme renewal — Dedicated GPU right-sizing & proposed add-on plan

Monica / Marissa — quick notes to surface for the call based on the CSV:

- Peak calc: Lisa, the "peak daily tail" is the 95th percentile of per-minute active GPU utilization across the last 90 days (we excluded scheduled maintenance windows). That captures burstiness without being driven by single anomalous minutes.
- Latency: With 56 committed and a 12-GPU burst pool (pre-warmed), model inference P50/P95 should remain within current SLOs for interactive traffic. We recommend setting a transient warm-up policy: keep 2 GPUs in warm state in the burst pool during business hours.
- Autoscale ceiling: keeping 80 as the temporary ceiling is conservative; if they want more cost savings we can test 72 and monitor queue depth.

I'll prepare a short slide with expected token-level cost delta for each config to share on the call.

- Dev
